They were joined by yet other members of the Club; Ben Challenger, who won the silver medal in the high jump, John Regis who took the bronze medal in the 200m, Du'aine Ladejo in the decathlon, Jason Lobo over 800m, Dave Smith in the hammer and Ian Tullett in the pole vault – all of these in the Engl…

High jump specialist Ben Challenger matched the height of winner Klyuigin but the Russian only needed two attempts to the Briton's three. Reserve pole vaulter Mike Edward had a late call and flew in from Waco, Texas, his kit not arriving until the night before his competition; he never looked comfor…

If he can throw 74.02 after training in a Dorking field, thanks to a helpful farmer, the best could yet be ahead of him. Silver for Ben Challenger That man Dalton Grant and our own Ben Challenger were the men leading the way in the high jump.

We had heard that the Yugoslav's were turning round anyone without Visa's, so the airlines were checking carefully all documents. The last problem came with the late replacement of Brendan Reilly by Ben Challenger. We flew Ben out JAL on the Saturday without a Visa.

No problems with the jumps squad until a week before departure, when Brendan Reilly was injured in a car crash and there was a last minute panic to get a visa for welcome newcomer Ben Challenger, who was now destined to make his début in a Belgrave vest in the high jump in Belgrade.

Ben Challenger made his League high jump début with a steady 2.20m. With Brendan Reilly still sidelined, suffering from whiplash injuries, Samson Oni got carried away in the exalted company and opened at 1.95m – which he failed to clear.
Ben Challenger competing for the first time since injuring himself in the Europa Cup, produced a stunning 2.26 to win the high jump but the Newham man was third.
